input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: The added `.strip()` removes all leading and trailing whitespace from the prompt, not just the ANSI codes that the change is meant to strip. A prompt such as "Name: " is passed to input() as "Name:", so the cursor sits directly against the colon.
- rationale: Trigger: a prompt whose text ends in a space (the usual form, e.g. click.prompt("Name", default=...) builds "Name: ") while should_strip_ansi is true, such as stdout piped or under CliRunner. The changed line strips the text, so func receives text without the trailing space. Impact: the rendered prompt loses its separator space and the output differs from the non-stripping path, so tests and users see a changed prompt.
critique: The finding identifies the same added .strip() following ANSI stripping. It describes the same effect: the trailing space in 'Name: ' is removed when should_strip_ansi is true (piped output or CliRunner), so the prompt renders differently from the non-stripping path.
